_meta.indication: Long-term, once-daily maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema. Not indicated for asthma or for acute deteriorations of COPD.

pivotal_trials.population: Patients 40 years or older with COPD, smoking history of at least 10 pack years, post-bronchodilator FEV1 less than 80% and at least 30% of predicted, and FEV1/FVC less than 70%
pivotal_trials.endpoint: 24-hour post-dose trough FEV1 after 12 weeks of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: Trough FEV1 at Week 12: indacaterol 75 mcg 1.38 L vs placebo 1.26 L; treatment difference 0.12 L (95% CI 0.08, 0.15)

pivotal_trials.population: Patients 40 years or older with COPD, smoking history of at least 10 pack years, post-bronchodilator FEV1 less than 80% and at least 30% of predicted, and FEV1/FVC less than 70%
pivotal_trials.endpoint: 24-hour post-dose trough FEV1 after 12 weeks of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: Trough FEV1 at Week 12: indacaterol 75 mcg 1.49 L vs placebo 1.35 L; treatment difference 0.14 L (95% CI 0.10, 0.18)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2% and more common than placebo) are cough, oropharyngeal pain, nasopharyngitis, headache and nausea. For 75 mcg vs placebo: cough 6.5% vs 4.5%, oropharyngeal pain 2.2% vs 0.7%, nasopharyngitis 5.3% vs 2.7%, headache 5.1% vs 2.5%, nausea 2.4% vs 0.9%. Most common serious adverse reactions were COPD exacerbation, pneumonia, angina pectoris, and atrial fibrillation.
target_moa: Indacaterol is a long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist that acts locally in the lung as a bronchodilator; stimulation of intracellular adenylyl cyclase increases cyclic AMP, causing relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ASTHMA-RELATED DEATH. Long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonists (LABA) increase the risk of asthma-related death. A placebo-controlled study with salmeterol showed an increase in asthma-related deaths; this is considered a class effect of LABA including indacaterol.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a Medication Guide and a communication plan regarding LABA safety of asthma-related death (Health Care Professional Letter, website information, and notification of professional societies).

advisory_committee.vote: Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) met March 8, 2011; by majority voting recommended approval of the 75 mcg dose (votes were 13 yes and 4 no); the added benefit of the 150 mcg dose was not considered demonstrated.

summary.text: Standard 505(b)(1) NDA for indacaterol maleate (Arcapta Neohaler) 75 mcg for COPD. The original NDA received a Complete Response letter on October 16, 2009; Novartis submitted a complete response on October 1, 2010. A Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee met March 8, 2011 and recommended approval of the 75 mcg dose (13 yes, 4 no). Approval was supported by a REMS with a Medication Guide and communication plan; no post-marketing study commitments were required.

citations.quote: Novartis originally submitted this 505(b)(1) new drug application for use of Arcalyst Neohaler (indacaterol maleate 150 mcg and 300 mcg dry powder for oral inhalation) for once-daily maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and emphysema.
The October 1, 2010, submission constituted a complete response to our October 16, 2009, action letter.

The Committee by majority voting concluded that efficacy for 75 mcg dose was demonstrated, that the 75 mcg was safe for use in COPD patients, and recommended approval of the 75 mcg dose (votes were 13 yes and 4 no).
The October 1, 2010, submission constituted a complete response to our October 16, 2009, action letter.

basis.text: Deficiencies communicated in the Complete Response letter; Novartis was asked to evaluate doses of indacaterol lower than 150 mcg and regimens with different dosing frequencies, and to provide replicate data showing a clinically meaningful advantage of a higher dose over a lower dose with balancing safety data.
